CONTEXT: A builder just stripped SFCC-89 functional additions out of a large TypeScript port so that the port can be committed on its own as a pure copy-first mechanical conversion. After that strip, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` must be a FAITHFUL TypeScript conversion of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx` and NOTHING MORE.

YOUR JOB — angle (b), scoped to `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` ONLY (a sibling is handling product-view). This is the core question of the commit.

Run exactly this normalisation diff (both flags are load-bearing: without `--with-node-modules` prettier skips the file; without `--config` it picks up retail-react-app's own prettier config and reproduces base formatting):

cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa && diff -u <(./node_modules/.bin/prettier --with-node-modules --config .prettierrc.yaml --parser typescript node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx) overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx

The builder reports this yields **333 changed lines across 28 hunks**. FIRST verify those two numbers precisely — state which measure you used (GNU `diff -u` changed-line count vs `git diff --no-index --numstat`; report BOTH so the number is unambiguous) and count hunks (`grep -c '^@@'`).

THEN — and this is the real work — **READ EVERY SINGLE HUNK** and classify each one into exactly one of:
  (A) pure TypeScript conversion (type annotations, `type`/`import type` declarations, generics, `as`/non-null assertions, replacing runtime `propTypes` with TS types, `.jsx`->`.tsx` import path changes)
  (B) house formatting / prettier config difference (quote style, indent, trailing comma, line width)
  (C) a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED deviation (there should be an in-file comment explaining it — quote the comment)
  (D) an eslint-disable comment or added explanatory comment required by the TS conversion
  (E) **ANYTHING ELSE — a surviving SFCC-89 functional addition, a behaviour change, a reordered/added/removed base code path, a changed prop, a changed default, a changed conditional, a changed JSX structure, a changed hook dependency array, a changed string literal, a dropped base feature.** Category (E) is a DEFECT or BLOCKER.

Be adversarial. Specific things to hunt:
- Any hunk where ours ADDS runtime code (not types, not comments) that base does not have.
- Any hunk where ours OMITS base runtime code. Especially check: every `useEffect`/`useMemo`/`useCallback` and its FULL dependency array; every einstein/datacloud analytics call; every `useProduct`/`useProducts`/`useShopperBasket` option object; the `<Seo>` block; the bundle/set handling branches; `handleAddToCart`/`handleAddToWishlist` bodies; the `<InformationAccordion>` / `<RecommendedProducts>` / `<Island>` blocks; `getServerSideProps`/`getTemplateName`/`getProps` statics and `ProductDetail.getTemplateName`/`.displayName`/`.propTypes` at the foot of the file.
- Any changed JSX nesting or changed Chakra prop that would shift layout (a prior review loop on this same work found an "ours-only layout-shift defect" that eight passes missed — hunt for a Chakra spacing/margin/padding/direction/display/align prop, a wrapper element, or a `<Stack>`/`<VStack>`/`<Box>` that exists in ours but not base, or vice versa).
- Any changed `data-testid`, `className`, `layerStyle`, `srOnly`, aria attribute, or role — these are behaviour/a11y, not formatting.
- Any changed default value, `??`/`||` fallback, or optional-chaining `?.` that base does not have (adding `?.` where base has `.` IS a behaviour change — it silences a throw; report each instance and whether it is documented in-file).
- Any import that resolves to a DIFFERENT module than base's (e.g. base imports from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view`, ours imports `'../../components/product-view'` — is that documented in-file? quote the comment).
- Blank-line-only and comment-only hunks are category (B)/(D); say so briefly and move on. Spend your budget on the hunks with real content.

Produce a HUNK-BY-HUNK TABLE: hunk number, ours line range, category (A-E), one-line justification. Then list every category (C), (D) and (E) hunk in full detail with quoted code.

OUTPUT: findings-first, ordered by severity: BLOCKER (wrong commit if shipped) / DEFECT (should fix now) / NOTE (record only) — then the hunk table. Every finding needs `absolute/file/path:line` and a label **CONFIRMED** (you reproduced it) or **PLAUSIBLE**. Then a short "What I could not verify" section naming what you could not reach and why. Do NOT run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx vitest`, `npm run lint`, or `npm run audit:tokens` — already run (0 tsc errors; 354/22 vitest pass; 17 lint err/16 warn; audit:tokens 14 unacknowledged). Do not write any report file into the repo — return findings as your final message text.

| Measure | Value |

The builder's "333 changed lines across 28 hunks" is exact under both measures.

## Method: I did not rely on the text diff alone

The text diff is dominated by prettier reflow, which hides real changes. So I also built an **AST-normalised comparison** (`@babel/parser` + `@babel/generator`, both files through the identical generator) that strips every type-only construct — `type` aliases, `import type`, type annotations, generics, `as`/`satisfies`/`!`, `this:` params — plus all comments and all whitespace-only `JSXText`. Anything surviving that is a genuine runtime difference.

**Result: the 28 text hunks collapse to exactly 9 runtime differences, and 7 of the 9 are provably behaviour-neutral.** Supporting sweeps, all clean:

- JSX **closing tags**: identical (`diff` exit 0)
- JSX **attribute names in document order**: 67 vs 67, **identical** (`diff` exit 0)
- **String literals**: only the 4 expected deltas (`product-view` path ×2, `'prop-types'` removed, two TS indexed-access literals)
- `data-testid` / `className` / `layerStyle` / `srOnly` / `aria-` / `role=` / `spacing` / `display` / `key`: identical counts

# FINDINGS (ordered by severity)

## No BLOCKERs

**No surviving SFCC-89 functional addition. No dropped base code path. No JSX structure, nesting, prop, prop-order, default, or string-literal change. No layout-shift defect in this file.** The `<Seo>`/`<Helmet>`, `<Island>`, `<InformationAccordion>`, `<RecommendedProducts>`, bundle/set branches, `handleAddToCart`/`handleAddToWishlist`/`handleProductBundleAddToCart` bodies, and every hook option object are all AST-identical to base.

Specifically on the layout-shift hunt: hunk 26 (`ours 721-792`) is the 72-line block where such a defect would live, and it looks alarming in the text diff because prettier re-indents the whole thing one level deeper. ## DEFECT 1 — Undocumented behaviour change: `?.` added to `ref.scrollIntoView`

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:513` — **CONFIRMED**

Base (`index.jsx:458`): `if (ref.scrollIntoView) {`

```tsx
    if (firstUnselectedProduct) {
      // Get the reference to the product view and scroll to it.
      const { ref } = childProductRefs.current[firstUnselectedProduct.id];

      if (ref?.scrollIntoView) {
```

The only comment in scope is the base file's own `// Get the reference to the product view and scroll to it.` There is **no deviation comment**. This is the third of exactly three `?.` additions in the file (verified by a comment-stripped operator census: base 65 → ours 69, `+4` operators = `type?.` ×2, `productItems?.` ×1, `ref?.` ×1) — and it is the **only one of the three the builder did not document**, while the other two got explicit "Deviation from the base file" comments. That inconsistency is the finding.

It is a real behaviour change: when `ref` is `null`, base throws a `TypeError` out of `handleChildProductValidation` (aborting add-to-cart with an unhandled error); ours falls through and `return false`s silently.

**Root cause — this is type-driven, not considered.** `tsconfig.json:26` sets `"strict": true`, and the builder typed `ChildProductRef.ref` as `HTMLDivElement | null` at `index.tsx:124`. That makes `ref.scrollIntoView` a `strictNullChecks` error, so `?.` was the path of least resistance to a green `tsc`.
